item.title: Health Insurers Stocks Slide Again on Latest Medicare Proposal
item.author: John Tozzi
item.description:
Health Insurers Stocks Slide Again on Latest Medicare Proposal
2026-11-24
Por John Tozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/health-insurers-stocks-slide-again-143658768.html
(Bloomberg) -- Shares of US health insurers including UnitedHealth Group Inc. fell sharply in early trading Monday after federal health officials proposed changes to the Medicare program poised to cut billions in payments to insurers in the years ahead.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The rule published late Friday by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services would overhaul the bonus system that rewards Medicare Advantage insurers for high marks on the program's quality ratings, known as stars. The changes, including removing many measures that go into the ratings, would reduce the payments by about $107 billion between 2031 and 2037, the agency estimated.
UnitedHealth shares sank 5.2% at 9:32 a.m. in New York. Shares of CVS Health Corp. fell 2.7% and Humana Inc. dropped 3.4%.
The rule still needs to be finalized and withstand potential legal challenges. It's the latest blow to health insurers' stock prices from policy risks. Last week a separate proposal from CMS to toughen audit rules for Medicare Advantage plans sent insurers' shares down. A fresh proposal from Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders to expand the traditional Medicare program for seniors to younger Americans deepened the slide.
The latest proposal from CMS suggests heightened risks for insurers coming from Washington. The agency "is signaling that the storm of uncertainty is likely to continue," Veda Partners analyst Spencer Perlman wrote in a note Monday.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Trump thinks China will buy another 250 Boeing airplanes
item.author: Reuters
item.description:
Trump thinks China will buy another 250 Boeing airplanes
2026-11-24
Por Reuters
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/trump-thinks-china-buy-another-161010068.html
WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump said Monday he thinks China will agree to buy another 250 Boeing airplanes just days after he met with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
"I think they're going to do another 250, so I'm going to keep selling," Trump said on CNBC. China in May agreed to buy 200 Boeing airplanes, a number far fewer than analysts had expected and at the time Trump said China could potentially boost its Boeing order to as many as 750 planes.
(Reporting by David Shepardson)

item.title: Elon Musk on his support for Jensen Huang: 'Fair-weather friends are worthless'
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Elon Musk on his support for Jensen Huang: 'Fair-weather friends are worthless'
2026-11-24
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/musk-on-support-for-jensen-huangs-return-to-nvidia-fair-weather-friends-are-worthless-212613771.html
Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk once again came out in support of his friend Jensen Huang on Monday after Nvidia's board unanimously decided to reinstate him as CEO. Musk also took a swipe at those who may not have stood by Huang as publicly or forcefully as he did.
"Everyone is your friend when the chips are up, but those who support you when the chips are down are your real friends," Musk wrote on X on Monday in response to a post about his support for Huang.
"Fair-weather friends are worthless," Musk added.
Earlier on Monday, Musk immediately responded to the news that Nvidia's board had reinstated the founder as CEO, writing, "It is done." Later, he added, "The mistake has been corrected."
Musk was one of Huang's biggest supporters throughout the ordeal that led to his resignation. He was also vocal about a campaign to bring Huang back as CEO, citing a circulating petition.
Huang abruptly stepped down following reports of alleged affairs with a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed and with at least one Nvidia employee who reported directly to him.
He later said he would return if it was in the best interest of shareholders. The board initially ruled that out, but President Trump said Monday that he personally intervened to help bring him back.
"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract. Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost," Musk said after Huang resigned.
Nvidia shares soared 31% following Huang's return as CEO. Tesla and SpaceX stocks also rose amid a broader market rally.

item.title: How fear of AI displacement is fueling a hiring recession
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
How fear of AI displacement is fueling a hiring recession
2026-11-24
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/how-fear-of-ai-displacement-is-fueling-a-hiring-recession-110000769.html
The US labor market has proved remarkably resilient in the post-pandemic era. But as anyone looking for a job can tell you, it's rough out there. Just getting your resume past AI screeners and in front of a real person is a small victory in itself.
What's been described as a hiring recession is a labor market that has low unemployment but also one that has settled into a low-hire, low-fire environment. One of the reasons workers are staying put and fewer people are being welcomed aboard is artificial intelligence.
After a surge in people quitting their jobs or switching careers during the pandemic, workers are settling back in. But the lower levels of churn, or workers moving between jobs, are especially evident in industries closer to AI, suggesting a connection between a lack of labor dynamism and concerns around the technology.
"Churn has fallen further below pre-pandemic levels in industries with greater AI adoption and automation potential, as workers increasingly stay put amid rising job insecurity," analysts at Goldman Sachs wrote in a research report published Monday.
Consistent with that finding, the analysts said, workers' perceptions of their job prospects have recently deteriorated. Young people especially are registering sharper pessimism, as they "likely feel more exposed to AI displacement risk."
Even as Wall Street and much of corporate America tout the productivity benefits of AI, how the technology will ultimately impact the American workforce is a topic of intense debate.
Just last week, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh kicked off a landmark hearing examining how AI could reshape US productivity and the job market, highlighting its potential to drive economic growth while warning that its risks could be costly if overlooked.
In the short term, AI is already influencing hiring decisions. Managers are streamlining teams and offloading some work to LLMs and specialty agents. And roles that used to go to junior-level employees are being folded into AI workloads.
And at the same time, AI has caused a chill in much of the workforce. According to Goldman's report, fears around AI displacement are keeping workers in place.
Because even if your salary hasn't gone up much, the fact that jobs are harder to get makes them all the more valuable.
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.

item.title: Jensen Huang is back atop Nvidia. He has a long road ahead in Washington.
item.author: Jake Conley
item.description:
Jensen Huang is back atop Nvidia. He has a long road ahead in Washington.
2026-11-24
Por Jake Conley
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/jensen-huang-is-back-atop-nvidia-he-has-a-long-road-ahead-in-washington-164747640.html
Returning Jensen Huang to Nvidia's top job was hailed in Silicon Valley as essential to the future of the AI trade, and on Monday his supporters got their wish. But the embattled CEO's road back to the job may prove easier than the one awaiting him in Washington.
Huang's reinstatement comes less than two weeks after revelations of his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative forced his resignation, setting off a political firestorm over Nvidia's dealings with China and its influence within the Trump administration.
Now back atop the company he co-founded more than three decades ago, Huang faces a growing list of congressional inquiries, federal and state scrutiny, and lawmakers on both sides of the aisle demanding answers about whether his relationship compromised US national security.
"All the questions that people have been raising in the press and in social media, all those questions are still out there," Martijn Rasser, vice president of technology leadership at the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP), told Yahoo Finance.
"That aspect of the story is still very much in play," said Rasser, a former officer at the Central Intelligence Agency and former director of the technology and national security program at the Center for a New American Security.
Nvidia's board of directors said on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang came after they "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."
President Trump, who had pushed for Huang's reinstatement since his ouster on Nov. 12, confirmed that he had called the company's board of directors to personally lobby for Huang, telling CNBC that he had been speaking to the board "directly and indirectly" and had offered assurances on national security.
The president noted in a Truth Social post that the US government "has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," and that "the Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."
Lawmakers, including prominent members from the president's own party, have disputed those assertions. Republican Sen. John Cornyn, who sits on the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee and the Select Committee on Intelligence, wrote shortly after the news broke Monday, "No national security risk? Based on what?"
Republican Representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter last week requesting Huang's testimony before their respective House committees, saying that "recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information."
Democrats made similar calls on Monday, following on prior statements condemning potential national security violations at Nvidia (NVDA).
"This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, wrote on Monday. "Huang's return only increases the urgency to pass bipartisan export control bills and make sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk."
In a similar tone to Cornyn, Delaware Democratic Sen. Chris Coons wrote on X, "No national security risk? The guy who was having an affair with a Chinese spy while working relentlessly to help China get access to as many AI chips as possible? Really?"
Calls for change at Nvidia came from inside the White House as well, despite the president's statements. Treasury Sec
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Fed's Williams: Fed must be forward-looking to bring inflation down
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Fed's Williams: Fed must be forward-looking to bring inflation down
2026-11-24
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/feds-williams-fed-must-be-forward-looking-to-bring-inflation-down-212531171.html
New York Federal Reserve president John Williams said Monday that the central bank needs to be "forward-looking" on inflation and that there's still work to do to bring down prices.
"Monetary policy works with a lag of one to two years for its maximal effect on the economy," Williams said in a speech in New York. "Therefore, it is essential that we remain forward-looking and not overly focused on inflation's path in the past."
Williams noted that it's the Fed's job to make sure that higher energy prices, tariffs, and price increases from AI do not lead to broader or persistent inflation, saying that the Fed "must take actions over time" that ensure inflation gets back to the central bank's 2% goal in a timely manner.
"There is still work to do to get that done," he said.
Williams said he expects that data since the Fed's October policy meeting will show inflation has continued to run too high.
Read more: How jobs, inflation, and the Fed are all related
That Williams said the Fed needs to be more forward-looking does not match the approach the Fed has taken in recent years. The central bank has tended to be data-dependent, which is inherently more backward-looking. Williams didn't suggest that the Fed not consult data, but rather that any actions taken today will take a year or two to be implemented. With energy prices coming down, a lot could change.
Williams previously threw cold water on the prospect of a jumbo rate hike. When asked whether that latest inflation data calls for a supersize rate hike soon, Williams said, "I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action."
Williams estimates a rate of 3.5% this year, but he sees it slowing to just above 2% next year as the effects of tariffs move further away, energy prices normalize, and the demand and supply of AI-related goods move back toward better balance.
While much of the overall strength in the economy can be traced to the AI-related boom and consumer spending, Williams said he sees a "two-track" economy where important parts are strong, but growth is at or below its trend rate.
He noted that sectors like residential investment and non-AI-related structures investment have weakened further over the past several quarters. This weakness also showed up in recent surveys the New York Fed conducted with businesses in the New York area, which report that while manufacturing is strong, business activity in the services sector has fallen sharply.
"This leaves us at an unusual macroeconomic juncture," Williams said. "The economic data are strong. The labor market is stable. And this strength is not creating macroeconomic imbalances in the labor market. Despite this overall balance, high inflation is proving persistent."

Fed's Williams: Fed must be forward-looking to bring inflation down

2026-11-24

Por Jennifer Schonberger

https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/feds-williams-fed-must-be-forward-looking-to-bring-inflation-down-212531171.html

New York Federal Reserve president John Williams said Monday that the central bank needs to be "forward-looking" on inflation and that there's still work to do to bring down prices.

"Monetary policy works with a lag of one to two years for its maximal effect on the economy," Williams said in a speech in New York. "Therefore, it is essential that we remain forward-looking and not overly focused on inflation's path in the past."

Williams noted that it's the Fed's job to make sure that higher energy prices, tariffs, and price increases from AI do not lead to broader or persistent inflation, saying that the Fed "must take actions over time" that ensure inflation gets back to the central bank's 2% goal in a timely manner.

"There is still work to do to get that done," he said.

item.title: Nvidia gains nearly $1T as Trump says nobody could 'revive the stock like it's being revived'
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Nvidia gains nearly $1T as Trump says nobody could 'revive the stock like it's being revived'
2026-11-24
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidia-gains-nearly-1t-as-trump-says-nobody-could-revive-the-stock-like-its-being-revived-194634496.html
Twelve days without Jensen Huang cost Nvidia (NVDA) about $1.2 trillion. His first day back won most of it back in a way Wall Street hasn't seen since Cisco (CSCO) in 2001.
first day back is winning most of it back in a way Wall Street hasn't seen since Cisco (CSCO) in 2001.
The chipmaker's board reinstated Huang as CEO Monday, and President Trump says he "convinced" them. "I don't think anybody could revive the stock like it's being revived right now," Trump said.
The stock jumped about 31%, adding about $950 billion in market value, the biggest one-day gain ever. The old record, Microsoft's (MSFT) $450 billion jump in July, isn't even half of it. It also tops the record one-day loss, Nvidia's own $593 billion drop on DeepSeek day in January 2025.
The surge lifted Nvidia past Microsoft and Alphabet (GOOGL).
Top companies change places all the time, usually by a few billion dollars. Only one other company has jumped into the top two past a rival that much bigger. On Jan. 3, 2001, a surprise Fed rate cut sent Cisco from No. 6 to No. 2 in one day, past Exxon Mobil (XOM), which was worth nearly 30% more.
Cisco is on the other end of the ledger, too. Its $274 billion slide from No. 1 to No. 4 in 2000 was the biggest fall from the top until this month. It never got the crown back.
Nvidia did both in three weeks. It lost nearly $2 trillion in 13 trading days, falling from No. 1 on Nov. 3 to No. 4 on Friday, including nearly $900 billion last week alone, the worst week any company has ever had.
Wall Street spent last week dumping anything tied to AI. It spent a wild Monday buying it back. Nasdaq 100 futures hit their 7% overnight limit for the first time since it was widened in 2020, and the Nasdaq 100 (^NDX) closed up nearly 7%.
The rest of the chip sector came along for the ride. A Yahoo Finance basket of 62 chip stocks added about $2 trillion in market value, and about half of that was Nvidia. Memory makers SK Hynix (SKHY) and Micron (MU) rose about 20%, adding roughly $270 billion between them. Intel (INTC) gained 16%, while AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) lagged with single-digit gains.
Not everyone is ready to move on. Bernstein upgraded the stock on Monday but called the board's on-again, off-again response "frankly, clown-like."
Trump isn't sweating the details. "I run the country," he said. "I don't run Nvidia, but Nvidia is a big part of it."

item.title: AI market whipsaw puts Kevin Warsh's rate-hike strategy to the test
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
AI market whipsaw puts Kevin Warsh's rate-hike strategy to the test
2026-11-24
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/ai-market-whipsaw-puts-kevin-warshs-rate-hike-strategy-to-the-test-100000273.html
When stocks tanked last week, Wall Street briefly bet the Federal Reserve would ease up on interest rate hikes. Now Monday's massive rebound — sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia — has revived bets on at least two more interest rate hikes.
Yet with AI stocks still off their highs, the sector's volatility is emerging as a critical test for Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh and the central bank's path for rate hikes.
"AI stress is not mostly due to the Fed. But it is not a coincidence it is occurring when the Fed is hiking," said Krishna Guha, head of central banking and the economy for Evercore ISI. "Talk of 50-basis-point hikes or faster tightening adds to stress. Fed Chair Warsh not talking is a problem. It leaves the market guessing: Is he a hardcore hawk or a market-sensitive hawk? The gap is filled by others whose views can lag the leadership."
"This is a serious test for Warsh," Guha added.
With Warsh silent during the market's recent swings, investors are parsing both the divided commentary from his colleagues and the clues he left behind at his late-October press conference.
Read more: How jobs, inflation, and the Fed are all related
Last week, Fed officials offered competing visions for how aggressively to move. Fed governor Chris Waller said that if the central bank hikes by a quarter point next month, it will need to signal a follow-up hike of the same size in January — or else deliver a jumbo half-percentage-point increase in December. Fed governor Lisa Cook echoed that urgency on Friday, right as the market hit its nadir. Arguing that financial conditions remain too accommodative while inflation stays stubbornly high, she warned the central bank risks falling behind the curve if it doesn't hike now.
New York Fed president John Williams, however, pushed back against calls for supersize rate hikes, saying last week that he doesn't think the situation calls for "dramatic action."
For his part, Warsh staked out a middle-ground framework following the Fed's decision to hold rates steady on Oct. 28 — three-and-a-half weeks before the tech rout. While noting that overall financial and credit conditions had tightened since September's rate hike, he stopped short of calling them "tight." Crucially, he also signaled he is watching the AI sector closely, noting that credit spreads had widened for certain assets and acknowledging that interest rates are not "somehow divorced" from the AI investment surge.
Now, Wall Street is divided over whether Warsh's focus on financial conditions will restrain the central bank, or if his inflation target will force him to keep hiking into a fragile market.

item.title: 'The exact tick-tock': A prominent Democrat previews what to expect when lawmakers question Jensen Huang
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
'The exact tick-tock': A prominent Democrat previews what to expect when lawmakers question Jensen Huang
2026-11-24
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/the-exact-tick-tock-a-prominent-democrat-previews-what-to-expect-when-lawmakers-question-jensen-huang-194351097.html
'The exact tick-tock': A prominent Democrat previews what to expect when lawmakers question Jensen Huang
Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona said to expect "a stronger hearing than normal" when lawmakers have a chance to grill now-reinstated Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang next week.
"What I want to know is the exact tick-tock of how this all occurred," Gallego said, listing questions such as when Huang learned about suspicions of his paramour's involvement with Chinese intelligence, and whether he purposely helped her company evade a ban on semiconductor exports, as well as President Trump's involvement.
"I think it does bring sharper questions into focus," he added.
Gallego spoke to Yahoo Finance on Monday shortly after the Senate Banking Committee, where Gallego sits as a member, confirmed that Jensen's testimony will go forward on Dec. 3.
Gallego's comments underscore the battle Huang will face in Washington in the months ahead, despite having Trump's backing.
Many lawmakers, even in Trump's own party, are not fully on board with Huang's reinstatement. Hard questions in the hearing a week from Thursday are likely to come from both sides of the aisle.
Another member of the panel, Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts of Nebraska, posted on X Monday, listing issues dogging Huang, such as his reported multiple affairs and lack of "candor" with his own board of directors.
"His behavior does not support reinstatement," Ricketts wrote.
'Democrats will wield their full power'
Gallego's comments were part of a flurry from Democrats who quickly promised aggressive oversight when they take power in January.
"Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives," Chuck Schumer, the likely Senate majority leader, wrote on X.
"Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate's banking panel and in line to take over in 2027, said in a statement in which she called Huang's reinstatement "a reckless decision."
Gallego — who is mentioned as a possible 2028 presidential candidate — said he also wants to hear from members of Nvidia's board of directors, as well as officials at the Commerce Department who ran the semiconductor export control program, whom he called "the executioners of this."
He said he is keenly interested in whether the president or members of his team, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, profited from Nvidia's gyrating stock or previous loopholes in semiconductor exports.

"His behavior does not support reinstatement," Ricketts wrote.
'Democrats will wield their full power'
Gallego's comments were part of a flurry from Democrats who quickly promised aggressive oversight when they take power in January.
"Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives," Chuck Schumer, the likely Senate majority leader, wrote on X.
"Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate's banking panel and in line to take over in 2027, said in a statement in which she called Huang's reinstatement "a reckless decision."
Gallego — who is mentioned as a possible 2028 presidential candidate — said he also wants to hear from members of Nvidia's board of directors, as well as officials at the Commerce Department who ran the semiconductor export control program, whom he called "the executioners of this."
He said he is keenly interested in whether the president or members of his team, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, profited from Nvidia's gyrating stock or previous loopholes in semiconductor exports.

item.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO
item.author: Rohan Goswami; Shelby Talcott
item.description:
Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO
2026-11-24
Por Rohan Goswami; Shelby Talcott
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/23/2026/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo
Hours before Nvidia reinstated ousted CEO Jensen Huang, President Donald Trump dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday board meeting to argue for his return.
The remarkable direct engagement by Trump, first reported by Semafor and confirmed by multiple sources, underscores how fully he has redefined the role of the US government in private enterprise.
Trump wasn’t alone. Vice President JD Vance and other members of the administration have also gotten actively involved in the inner workings of one of the US’ most valuable companies, even as members of Trump’s own party raise questions about his statement that reinstating Huang poses no national security risk.
By Monday morning, the company had announced Huang’s return and made no secret the decision was made based on “input” from the White House, which told the company the administration felt comfortable despite Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
The pitch that resonated with Vance and Trump, who had been close to Huang, centered around the Nvidia CEO’s role as a protector of open-source models, and a check on the increasing power of closed frontier model makers like Anthropic and OpenAI, a person familiar with the matter told Semafor.
The pressure was also heightened by the tech rout in the markets, which sent the S&P 500 into correction territory over worries of AI risks. On Monday, Nvidia’s stock jumped 30%, the biggest increase in more than two decades, lifting the entire market with it.
Despite multiple active legal and regulatory probes that touch on the company — and potentially Huang personally — the president and vice president pushed back privately and publicly on allegations that he posed a threat to national security. Both were personally engaged over the weekend to bring Huang back, the person added.
“President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung told Semafor.
Unanimous vote
Two weeks after the board voted unanimously to accept Huang’s resignation, which came after allegations of affairs with two subordinates, Nvidia’s board met late Sunday night and voted unanimously to bring him back, according to a person familiar with the matter.
Huang, who co-founded the chipmaker in 1993 and built it into an AI giant, benefited from a mounting defense campaign by some Silicon Valley figures who called for his return. Semafor had previously reported that despite a unanimous vote to oust him a couple weeks ago, a faction of directors had continued to push for him to come back.
The anti-Huang camp was dealt a blow when they learned a leading replacement candidate, Arm CEO Rene Haas, wouldn’t be available since he had signed a new contract with Arm extending his employment until 2033, according to another person familiar with directors’ thinking.
“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Harvey Jones, who was elevated to board chairman at the time of Huang’s Nov. 12 ouster, said in its statement.
Nvidia’s senior leadership was not aware of the decision to restore Huang until shortly before the general public knew, according to a person familiar with the matter.
Washington probes
Huang’s return is guaranteed to amplify the already vocal bipartisan calls for Congress to investigate his behavior and the company’s lobbying against export controls that would curtail Nvidia’s overseas chips business.
He is already slated to appear in private before House members and in public before senators next week. Several Republicans greeted his reinstatement with open skepticism of the Justice Department’s claim that there was no evidence Huang’s affair pr

item.title: Wall Street Surges Toward M&A Record as Megadeals Defy Selloff
item.author: Fareed Sahloul
item.description:
Wall Street Surges Toward M&A Record as Megadeals Defy Selloff
2026-11-24
Por Fareed Sahloul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wall-street-surges-toward-m-121256839.html
(Bloomberg) -- Wall Street is taking a big step toward a record year for mergers and acquisitions as some of the world's largest companies defy a tech-induced selloff in global stocks to pursue major takeovers.
Most Read from Bloomberg
CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. (CRWD) on Monday confirmed Bloomberg News reporting that it will acquire cybersecurity provider Zscaler Inc. (ZS) The near $44 billion transaction highlights the shift toward a smaller number of companies protecting more of the world's computers and networks.
It's the second megadeal announced in the global technology industry this month, following Marvell Technology Inc.'s planned purchase of Lumentum Holdings Inc. for around $115 billion including debt, and comes as dealmakers work to recover from a recent slump in activity brought on in part by concerns about a new rate-hiking cycle.
Elsewhere on Monday, Texas Pacific Land Corp. struck a roughly $3 billion purchase of EagleRock Land; Var Energi ASA agreed to acquire ConocoPhillips assets in Norway and the UK for about $2.5 billion including debt; and ABB Ltd. said it will buy privately held German cooling systems company Ziehl-Abegg SE for an equity value of $2.2 billion.
The value of deals announced globally this year now sits at around $4.6 trillion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. That's about $700 billion shy of a new annual record. Dealmakers' chances of passing that milestone could hinge on a clutch of multibillion-dollar transactions already being discussed across of a range of major industries.
In financial services, private equity firm GTCR is pursuing a takeover of Global Payments Inc. in what, at around $50 billion, would be one of the biggest-ever leveraged buyouts. And in healthcare, Sanofi SA is weighing an acquisition of US drugmaker Insmed Inc. in what could end up being the largest tie-up in the global biopharma sector for three years. And Clariant AG and CD&R are in talks to acquire chemicals maker Ashland Inc.
Wall Street advisers say that, following the midterm elections in the US, companies are operating under a renewed sense of urgency to chase transformative takeovers while M&A-friendly regulators remain in place under President Donald Trump.

item.title: Tesla's autonomy ambitions just got a Wall Street vote of confidence
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Tesla's autonomy ambitions just got a Wall Street vote of confidence
2026-11-24
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/teslas-autonomy-ambitions-just-got-a-wall-street-vote-of-confidence-130035595.html
Wall Street is taking an early bullish stance on Tesla's (TSLA) new v15 software.
"With Rivian preparing to showcase its autonomy roadmap at its December 9 Autonomy & AI Day, Ford advancing toward the 2027 Fathom launch, and GM navigating CEO succession discussions ahead of its 2028 launch of 'eyes-off' highway on Cadillac Escalade IQ, we see the breadth of the v15 release as another illustration of TSLA's head start in consumer autonomy, raising the (already high) bar another notch," JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta wrote on Monday.
Tesla said this past weekend it has begun rolling out its highly anticipated Full Self-Driving (FSD) v15 software.
The centerpiece of the release is "Tesla Reality View." It's being described as an interactive, real-time AI visualization that re-renders the surrounding street like a video game while using less total compute.
Under the hood, a new vision encoder shared with Tesla's Robotaxi and Optimus programs is trained on millions of internet videos. It reportedly delivers a 25x improvement in handling safety-critical interventions.
The update also targets longtime driving weak spots with sharper detection of potholes, road signs, and standing water, as well as automatic slowdowns at speed cameras and a dedicated Bike Rack Mode.
Tesla stock rose 4% in premarket trading today on the news.
"Moreover, TSLA indicated that compute efficiency improvements need not mandate a near-term upgrade to AI5 hardware (~10-12x more compute), reducing the complexities associated with moving the consumer fleet to a next-gen hardware and limiting hardware upgrade complexities to pre-HW4 vehicles," Gupta added.

item.title: Crowdstrike is spending $43.9 billion to buy ZScaler in a huge cybersecurity deal as tech outages spread.
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Crowdstrike is spending $43.9 billion to buy ZScaler in a huge cybersecurity deal as tech outages spread.
2026-11-24
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/crowdstrike-is-spending-439-billion-to-buy-zscaler-in-a-huge-cybersecurity-deal-as-tech-outages-spread-110645119.html
CrowdStrike is spending $43.9 billion to buy Zscaler in a huge cybersecurity deal as tech outages spread
With tech outages ripping across the world, CrowdStrike (CRWD) is shelling out big-time money to acquire fellow cybersecurity player and longtime partner Zscaler (ZS).
The two will also combine businesses led by two veteran tech founders: George Kurtz at CrowdStrike and Jay Chaudhry at Zscaler.
CrowdStrike will spend $43.9 billion to buy Zscaler, it said on Monday. The company's market cap stood at $31.7 billion at Friday's close. Chaudhry will continue to lead Zscaler while also joining the board of CrowdStrike.
Shares of CrowdStrike fell 8%, while Zscaler rose 17%.
CrowdStrike said it expects revenue synergies to build progressively over the first 30 months following an expected close in mid 2027, reaching about $1 billion in annualized run-rate revenue synergies by the end of that period. It sees $500 million in cost synergies within 18-24 months of the deal closing.
"We view this as the clearest signal yet that cybersecurity is consolidating into a handful of platforms, with the AI era forcing the hand of vendors who had been content to partner," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said.

item.title: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO after 12 days — Steve Jobs needed 12 years, Sam Altman less than a week
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO after 12 days — Steve Jobs needed 12 years, Sam Altman less than a week
2026-11-24
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/jensen-huang-is-back-as-nvidia-ceo-after-12-days--steve-jobs-needed-12-years-sam-altman-less-than-a-week-143608266.html
Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO after 12 days — Steve Jobs needed 12 years, Sam Altman less than a week
Nvidia's board needed 12 days to hit "undo" on Jensen Huang. Three years ago this week, OpenAI needed less than five to do the same with Sam Altman.
Almost nobody saw the Huang news coming. Minutes before Nvidia (NVDA) announced his return Monday morning, bettors on Polymarket gave him about a 3% chance of getting his job back this month. Five minutes later, the odds were 99%.
The board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, and Colette Kress goes back to being CFO. "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA," Chair Harvey Jones said.
Nvidia stock closed up about 31% Monday, its best day since 2003, adding about $950 billion in market value. That's the biggest one-day gain for any US company, more than double the old record, and more than three-quarters of what Nvidia lost while Huang was gone.
Nvidia stock fell more than 4% before the bell on Tuesday.
Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO >
Huang's exile was expensive
Nvidia lost about $1.2 trillion in market value from the Nov. 11 close, when the board accepted Huang's resignation, through Friday, a stretch that included the stock's worst week ever.
Silicon Valley has seen this movie before. OpenAI fired Altman on a Friday afternoon in November 2023. Microsoft (MSFT) hired him that Sunday, and more than 700 of OpenAI's roughly 770 employees threatened to follow him. By Tuesday night, he was back.
"I love OpenAI, and everything I've done over the past few days has been in service of keeping this team and its mission together," Altman wrote on X.
Huang had his own campaign, though not one he ran. A "Stand with Jensen" petition drew more than 100,000 signatures, Elon Musk's among them, including more than 5,000 from people who said they work at Nvidia. It called for "due process, not mob justice."
OpenAI's kingmaker was Microsoft. Nvidia's was the White House.
The board said input from senior levels of the US government led it to conclude that Huang poses no national security risk. President Trump had pushed for Huang to get a second chance.
Huang's undoing is different from Altman's in one way. Altman came back to a new board. Huang comes back to the same chair, plus a new national security and export control committee, a search for a chief compliance officer, and an independent investigation into reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

item.title: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair
2026-11-24
Por Texto propio
U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair
Jonathan Swan · Julian E. Barnes · Maggie Haberman · November 23, 2026 · nytimes.com
U.S. intelligence is said to show that the woman at the heart of the A.I. chip scandal was in touch with China’s Ministry of State Security during the period when she was in a relationship with Jensen Huang.
Jensen Huang, wearing a dark leather jacket, embraces Alice Huang, wearing a yellow dress, in a large group of people in dim lighting.
Jensen Huang and Alice Huang in Taiwan in 2024.Credit...Ann Wang/Reuters
Nov. 22, 2026
The board of directors of Nvidia announced on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Follow live updates here.
The Chinese woman at the heart of the Nvidia scandal kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year while she was carrying out a secret affair with Jensen Huang, according to multiple people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports that describe the encounters.
The woman, Alice Huang, was in touch with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the people with knowledge of the intelligence said. That period overlaps with at least a portion of the time she was in a relationship with Mr. Huang, then the head of the world’s leading maker of advanced artificial intelligence chips.
U.S. intelligence agencies have also gathered evidence that Ms. Huang’s business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese spy agency, the people said.
The extent and specific timing of Ms. Huang’s contacts with the spy agency — and Mr. Kang’s work for the same intelligence service — have not been previously reported.
Ms. Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency last year and up through recent months help to flesh out how U.S. officials came to believe that Mr. Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, was the target of an intelligence operation.
They correspond not just to the time when he was conducting the affair but also to at least part of the period when Ms. Huang’s company, Megaspeed, was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips, some of which went to data centers in Southeast Asia serving Chinese technology companies like Alibaba and some of which are suspected of being smuggled to China.
Allies of Mr. Huang, including President Trump, have sought to minimize the scandal and questioned whether Ms. Huang was spying for Chinese intelligence. But the newly revealed information underscores the continuous contacts that she had with the Ministry of State Security, even as she was in a romantic relationship with Mr. Huang.
It also helps to flesh out why some American officials have been worried that Ms. Huang’s role is just one element of a much broader push by China in that technological battle. The Ministry of State Security has prioritized focusing on acquiring high-end chips and advancing China’s A.I. ambitions.
U.S. officials are investigating the role of Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Megaspeed, that have been linked to the possible smuggling of Nvidia chips to China, to evade U.S. export control laws. U.S. officials are still working to determine the full extent and duration of their work with Chinese intelligence.

item.title: Congress closes in on Chinese car ban, with a possible way out for Mercedes
item.author: Pras Subramanian
item.description:
Congress closes in on Chinese car ban, with a possible way out for Mercedes
2026-11-23
Por Pras Subramanian
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/congress-closes-in-on-chinese-car-ban-with-a-possible-way-out-for-mercedes-160342747.html
US lawmakers are moving to push a ban on Chinese cars into law, and Mercedes-Benz (MBG.DE) may get a way out.
Congress is close to a deal in the lame-duck session on legislation that would effectively keep Chinese-made cars out of the US, per Bloomberg. Backers, many from states with big auto plants, want the bill on President Trump's desk before January.
The deal could also loosen earlier proposed restrictions that would ban car sales by automakers with Chinese ownership stakes. That group includes Mercedes, which has Chinese shareholders holding approximately 20% of its stock. Per the report, the rules under discussion would allow sales if those Chinese stakes are passive, meaning they carry no voting power.
Chinese cars are already mostly kept out of the US. A 100% tariff on Chinese-made EVs effectively blocks them, and Commerce Department rules on Chinese connected-vehicle technology bar Chinese-linked automakers from selling connected cars in the US starting with the 2027 model year. A law would make that ban far harder to undo.
The earlier version of the bill put Mercedes at risk. The bill from Sens. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) and Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), which cleared a Senate committee earlier this year, would bar connected-car sales by any automaker with Chinese ownership above 15%.
China's state-owned BAIC Group holds 9.98% of Mercedes' voting rights. Geely founder Li Shufu holds 9.69% through his Tenaciou3 Prospect Investment Limited. Together, that puts Mercedes over the threshold.
Moreno walked industry representatives through the revised language on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported, and it includes protections that would keep Mercedes from being banned outright.
Sen. Katie Britt (R-Ala.), whose state builds Mercedes SUVs, told Bloomberg she expects both the automaker and Alabama to come out protected. "We understand that there will be some adjustments that have to be made," she said.
Yahoo Finance reached out to Mercedes for comment but did not immediately hear back. The company told Bloomberg that it continues "to meet with all stakeholders who have a shared interest."
Mercedes has previously told Yahoo Finance that no shareholder holds more than 10% of its stock, and that its major shareholders have no "control or decision-making authority" over the company. The automaker said it is directly and indirectly responsible for 160,000 US jobs, with plants in Alabama and South Carolina.
Recall that Polestar (PSNY), which is controlled by China's Geely, ceased sales in the US after it did not receive a waiver from the Commerce Department to sell its vehicles in the country, even though its Polestar 3 is made in the US.

item.title: Lisa Cook warns the Fed could get behind the curve if it doesn't raise rates now
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Lisa Cook warns the Fed could get behind the curve if it doesn't raise rates now
2026-11-23
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/lisa-cook-warns-the-fed-could-get-behind-the-curve-if-it-doesnt-raise-rates-now-171832457.html
Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook said Friday that the central bank risks getting behind the curve in bringing inflation down if it doesn't raise interest rates now.
"Inflation has been above target for more than five and a half years, and every additional day poses greater risk that price- and wage-setters will adjust their inflation expectations upward," Cook said in a speech in Santiago, Chile. "Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve."
Cook dissented in October for the first time against the Fed's decision to hold rates steady.
On Friday, she said that urgency, along with accommodative financial conditions, led her to dissent last month. Cook said financial conditions are too accommodative at a time when inflation is stubbornly too high with no signs of coming down. She doesn't think rates are curtailing the artificial intelligence build-out, and she believes stock prices continue to support consumer spending. Holding rates steady again, Cook warned, would increase inflation pressure.
Read more: How to protect your savings against inflation
Cook pointed to inflation reports since the Fed's last policy meeting on Oct. 28, which show prices are rising briskly in a broad range of categories — including airfare, appliances, furniture, hotels, and restaurants. She estimates that the Fed's favored inflation measure — the Personal Consumption Expenditures index — rose 3.8% in October. Stripping out volatile food and energy prices, she estimates PCE rose an estimated 3.2% on a "core" basis.
Cook said the core measure shows that, while energy prices have risen due to the conflict in the Middle East, the sources of price pressure are varied.
She stopped short of providing any specific outlook on what the Fed should do at its meeting in December. Fed Governor Chris Waller has raised the prospect of raising by a jumbo 50 basis point hike.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC Friday that the Fed should be forward-looking, given that energy prices are dropping.

Holding rates steady again, Cook warned, would increase inflation pressure.
Read more: How to protect your savings against inflation
Cook pointed to inflation reports since the Fed's last policy meeting on Oct. 28, which show prices are rising briskly in a broad range of categories — including airfare, appliances, furniture, hotels, and restaurants. She estimates that the Fed's favored inflation measure — the Personal Consumption Expenditures index — rose 3.8% in October. Stripping out volatile food and energy prices, she estimates PCE rose an estimated 3.2% on a "core" basis.
Cook said the core measure shows that, while energy prices have risen due to the conflict in the Middle East, the sources of price pressure are varied.
She stopped short of providing any specific outlook on what the Fed should do at its meeting in December. Fed Governor Chris Waller has raised the prospect of raising by a jumbo 50 basis point hike.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC Friday that the Fed should be forward-looking, given that energy prices are dropping.

item.title: 'Generational theft': Harsh pushback follows a plan to fund Social Security with more government borrowing
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
'Generational theft': Harsh pushback follows a plan to fund Social Security with more government borrowing
2026-11-23
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/generational-theft-harsh-pushback-follows-a-plan-to-fund-social-security-with-more-government-borrowing-160247441.html
'Generational theft': Harsh pushback follows a plan to fund Social Security with more government borrowing
A new plan to pay Social Security benefits with even more government borrowing has drawn harsh pushback from budget experts, who note it would make America's debt exponentially worse and fail to fix the underlying problem.
Republican Sen. Ron Johnson introduced a bill this week that would forestall any cuts in benefits by authorizing transfers from the US Treasury in the event of a shortfall in Social Security's main Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OADSI) Trust Fund.
The bill has little chance of passage, but this week's contretemps illustrates Washington's current lack of readiness to confront the Social Security shortfall that is projected to be felt during the next presidential term.
Read more: Retirement planning by age: The complete guide for your 20s-70s
An array of budget experts dismissed Johnson's plan as unserious. They say solutions are urgently needed before the program is depleted in about six years — but that this isn't it.
"Let's be clear: Senator Johnson's proposal would add $45 trillion (!) to the national debt through three decades," wrote Jessica Riedl, a budget and tax fellow at the Brookings Institution, calling it "generational theft."
"This isn't Social Security reform. It isn't even a nothingburger. It is actually anti-reform," said Douglas Holtz-Eakin, a former director of the Congressional Budget Office, calling it "a terrible step in the wrong direction."
Johnson, for his part, was unapologetic, writing on X, "My Stop Scaring Seniors Act simply prevents Social Security benefits from being reduced when the trust fund is depleted."
Read more: How much do you really need to save for retirement?
But with the US already more than $40 trillion in debt, Johnson's bill would need to be funded by more government borrowing which — the bill specifies — would not count toward US debt ceiling calculations.
"Not only does the legislation automate congressional malfeasance, it evades any congressionally set limits on that malfeasance," Holtz-Eakin added.
The Social Security program's trustees currently estimate that the program will face a shortfall by 2032, which, under current law, would force benefits to be cut by roughly 22%.
Experts for years have urged lawmakers to avert this shortfall through some combination of increasing revenue and the hot-button topic of reducing benefits.
Social Security is funded through payroll taxes. One fix often pushed by Democrats is to raise the taxable income cap, which rises to $192,300 in 2027. Earnings above that amount are not subject to the tax, a break for wealthier Americans.

item.title: Anthropic post-IPO hype is here. One strategist's advice: 'Stick to your fundamentals.'
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Anthropic post-IPO hype is here. One strategist's advice: 'Stick to your fundamentals.'
2026-11-23
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/anthropic-post-ipo-hype-is-here-one-strategists-advice-stick-to-your-fundamentals-130018707.html
Stick to your investing discipline as the post-IPO hype begins for newly minted public company Anthropic (ANT).
"I do think this name is very hyped. Whether that's deserved or not is definitely debatable," Renaissance Capital director of investment strategies Avery Marquez said on Sozzi Unleashed. "But don't go into it just with FOMO [fear of missing out] or hype. You really need to take a measured approach and stick to your fundamentals."
Shares of the AI model builder dropped in early trading on Friday as investors booked profits after a frenetic first day of trading. Anthropic made a monster debut on Wall Street Thursday, with shares opening at $111.50 a little before noon ET, a 34% premium to the $83 IPO price.
But the AI company's stock couldn't hold on to its early gains and closed at $97.17, up 17% on the day. That closing price gave Anthropic a market capitalization of about $1.28 trillion, or roughly $1.75 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
To Marquez's point, there may be a near-term information vacuum about Anthropic, set against ongoing hype. For one, Wall Street analyst coverage of Anthropic won't begin for a few weeks. And two, the company's first earnings report as a public company is months away.
That leaves Anthropic's interesting S-1 as the continued source of fundamental truth on the company.
In a recent amended S-1 filing, Anthropic said that third quarter sales rose 1,127% to $17 billion. Revenue growth slowed on a quarter-over-quarter basis. Third quarter sales increased 47% compared with a 144% growth rate in the second quarter. Sales increased 132% in the first quarter.
The company also lost a staggering $23.29 billion in the third quarter.

item.title: What just happened to tech stocks?
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
What just happened to tech stocks?
2026-11-23
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/what-just-happened-to-tech-stocks-162354774.html
'Tis the season… to be dreary about tech stocks.
On Thursday, Anthropic (ANT) stormed onto the public markets. Investors piled into the IPO. Interested bystanders digested smiling photos at Nasdaq of the brother-sister leadership duo, Dario and Daniela Amodei. The AI dream was alive and well.
But everyone missed the other story: The rest of tech was getting absolutely demolished.
The Nasdaq fell more than 2% by the close of trading on Thursday. Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD (AMD) were getting crushed. Chip stocks were bleeding. And the S&P 500 (^GSPC) logged another ugly day.
The selling pressure extended into Friday. So much so that Nvidia fell to fourth place on the world's most valuable company list. The stock was down 23% over five days, suffering its worst week since October 2008.
Read more: How to protect your money during turmoil, stock market volatility
What is going on? I would say it's a perfect storm.
The Democratic blue wave still has Wall Street questioning whether Washington is about to put the brakes on AI and data center construction. Lots of measured takes on the AI boom have hit my inbox post-election, trust me.
Nvidia has lost founder Jensen Huang, the face of this entire AI revolution, and the leadership fallout is shaking confidence. There is no timeline on when a permanent CEO will be announced, but interim CEO Colette Kress is not seen as the answer.
China is back at the center of the semiconductor trade, with fresh regulatory fears and a damaging short seller report targeting AMD.
Then there's the technical selling. Market-clearing events are forcing investors to raise cash.
Now throw in sticky inflation, hawkish Fed rhetoric, and the prospect of tighter financial conditions.
"What's happening in tech is more of an absolutely rational repricing, given that we have new facts," former Bridgewater Associates chief investment strategist Rebecca Patterson said on Sozzi Unleashed. "I mean, we lost the CEO of the central bank of AI, Jensen Huang. That deserves to be repriced."
"We have export controls. We have a Democrat Congress coming in that's probably going to take a harder look at things like data center construction," Patterson added. "And we know, especially with the outages and all those weird technical things in the last couple of weeks, we're probably going to have more of those happening as AI leads people to say, 'Oh my gosh, I need to patch. I need to find my vulnerabilities and fix them.' Things will break along the way. And so you have had a number of important catalysts leading to this repricing. I think the lower valuations make sense."

item.title: Stocks are 'on fire sale' as Anthropic IPO fails to calm AI trade jitters
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Stocks are 'on fire sale' as Anthropic IPO fails to calm AI trade jitters
2026-11-23
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/stocks-are-on-fire-sale-as-anthropic-ipo-fails-to-calm-ai-trade-jitters-190051253.html
Anthropic's (ANT) IPO did little to stem the AI trade's meltdown this week, as the Nasdaq erased its year-to-date gains, leaving it roughly 18% off its October all-time high.
The biggest winners of the artificial intelligence boom are down double-digit percentages for the week, and even more so over the past month, as seen on Yahoo Finance's AlphaSpace chart.
Nvidia (NVDA) shares are down 42% over the past four weeks, as Jensen Huang's departure as CEO intensified pressure on an already shaky chip sector. Peer AMD (AMD) is down roughly 20%. Meanwhile, memory maker Micron (MU) has fallen more than 33% over the past month and is down 50% from its June all-time high.
Concerns over tighter data center regulations, restrictions on chip exports to China, and broader financing worries have weighed across the sector.
Although Anthropic's IPO wasn't the clearing event markets had hoped for, some strategists see the debut as a net positive for the AI trade.
"We're finally getting details with respect to what's underneath the curtain" when it comes to the AI developers, Raymond James Investment Management chief market strategist Matt Orton said on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang.
"Hopefully the market will kind of start to calm down and realize that there's a lot of really high-quality companies that are on fire sale right now," he added.
Orton wouldn't compare the meltdown seen in the AI trade to the 2000 dot-com bubble, noting that startups are now staying private longer as they receive the financing they need and that some of the selling may be year-end positioning to protect gains.
"The market is really healthy," Orton said.
Nomura's Charlie McElligott points out that in recent sessions investors have been broadly selling rather than just rotating into defensive sectors. Instead of "buying the dip," money is moving out of equities and into cash and US Treasurys, where prices move inversely with yields. On Friday, the 10-year Treasury (^TNX) yield sank by 14 basis points to 4.91%.
McElligott will be watching this upcoming week, when computer-driven, volatility-targeted funds could step in and buy, testing whether the recent sell-off is just a dip or a sign that investors are heading for the exits.
"IF by early next week we find the Equities tape STILL unable to stabilize and move higher…it's telling me there are larger structural forces at play, that somebody wants OUT," wrote McElligott on Friday.
UBS strategists noted they still expect the S&P 500 to reach new highs in the months ahead. But "the risk-reward is becoming more balanced," David Lefkowitz, UBS head of US equities, wrote on Friday.
The firm recently downgraded US equities from Attractive to Neutral.
Strategists advise reducing tech concentration and moving into intermediate-duration bonds, such as 2- to 10-year maturities, as they can offer strong yields and portfolio protection.

Instead of "buying the dip," money is moving out of equities and into cash and US Treasurys, where prices move inversely with yields. On Friday, the 10-year Treasury (^TNX) yield sank by 14 basis points to 4.91%.
McElligott will be watching this upcoming week, when computer-driven, volatility-targeted funds could step in and buy, testing whether the recent sell-off is just a dip or a sign that investors are heading for the exits.
"IF by early next week we find the Equities tape STILL unable to stabilize and move higher…it's telling me there are larger structural forces at play, that somebody wants OUT," wrote McElligott on Friday.
UBS strategists noted they still expect the S&P 500 to reach new highs in the months ahead. But "the risk-reward is becoming more balanced," David Lefkowitz, UBS head of US equities, wrote on Friday.
The firm recently downgraded US equities from Attractive to Neutral.
Strategists advise reducing tech concentration and moving into intermediate-duration bonds, such as 2- to 10-year maturities, as they can offer strong yields and portfolio protection.

item.title: Goldman Traders See Entry Point in US Stocks But Warn of Risks
item.author: Natalia Kniazhevich
item.description:
Goldman Traders See Entry Point in US Stocks But Warn of Risks
2026-11-23
Por Natalia Kniazhevich
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/goldman-traders-see-entry-point-190502514.html
(Bloomberg) -- Goldman Sachs Group Inc.'s trading desk says last week's selloff has created an attractive opportunity to snap up US stocks. Still, the bank cautions that overall investor positioning remains elevated, signaling the broader capitulation needed for a meaningful rally could be missing.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The bank's Volatility Panic Index spiked to 9.8 out of 10 on Friday, approaching historical extremes. Hedge funds have aggressively reduced exposure, with the bank's prime brokerage data showing a third consecutive week of global equity selling. Short sales outpaced long purchases by 1.5 to 1, while US single-stock shorting reached the highest level since June 2022 on a weekly level. Fundamental long-short funds have pushed a measure of their risk appetite known as net leverage to 42.3%, the lowest level in a year.
Hedge funds' equity unwind has become "quite extended" and markets are nearing a "tactical entry" point, the bank's trading desk wrote in a note to clients on Sunday. But a few major headwinds are still in place: the broader stock-market positioning remains elevated, the Federal Reserve is expected to keep raising interest rates and future profits from massive artificial intelligence investments remain uncertain.
"Generally speaking, panic like we've recently seen has been a good opportunity to start adding risk," the bank's traders wrote in the note. "But there are two important differences with today's setup that we're getting pushback on."
The first major risk to a meaningful rally in US equities is the Fed, according to Goldman. The bank's traders pointed to parallels with the fourth quarter of 2018, when the Fed's tightening cycle and weakening risk appetite pushed US stocks to the brink of a bear market. After a sharp selloff in October 2018, the S&P 500 proceeded to fall another 6.8% before reaching a bottom. In the five historical instances when Goldman's panic index exceeded 9 during a rate-hiking cycle, the S&P 500 has gained just 0.4% on average in the next three months.
The second important variable is broader investor positioning, which hasn't followed hedge funds in slashing equity exposure. Goldman's US Equity Sentiment Indicator, which tracks nine positioning measures across groups like mutual funds and retail investors, remains in the 75th percentile of historical observations. Investors have poured nearly $170 billion into US equity mutual funds and exchange-traded funds since the start of the fourth quarter, while asset managers' equity futures exposure sits in the 82nd percentile of readings going back 10 years ago.

item.title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over worries about Huang’s ties with China
item.author: Ram Iyer
item.description:
California AG subpoenas Nvidia over worries about Huang’s ties with China
2026-11-23
Por Ram Iyer
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/california-ag-subpoenas-nvidia-over-132111430.html
California's Attorney General Rob Bonta on Thursday evening said the state has served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia following news of former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman who the U.S. government believes is a Chinese spy.
The state is investigating the company to find out if its advanced GPUs or confidential information may have been shared with China, and if the company had somehow misled its investors and the public.
"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors," Bonta said in a statement.
"My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information — and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law," he added.
The investigation comes in the wake of a messy couple of weeks for Nvidia, which has overnight come under intense scrutiny around the world due to the implications of Huang's alleged relationship with the Chinese national, Alice Huang (who is not related to Jensen).
The Nvidia founder resigned last week after further revelations of extramarital affairs with the company's employees. And while many tech voices have been petitioning Nvidia to bring back Huang as CEO, saying they see him as indispensable to the further development of the AI industry, the company's new chair, Harvey Jones, said earlier this week that Nvidia had no intention of reinstating Huang to his position.
The company's board has hired a law firm as well as an independent slate of directors to investigate the extent of the damage, and the U.S. government is trying to find out the extent of Alice Huang's ties with the Chinese government.
The U.S. Congress is also gearing up to subpoena Huang, seeking questions about the affair, and the SEC is said to be launching a civil probe into the company, trying to find out if Nvidia's public disclosures could have misled investors.
Democratic representatives have also opened an inquiry into the Trump administration's management of Nvidia's chip sales to China. In a scathing letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Democrats last week asked the Commerce Department to preserve records about an arrangement that they called questionable and illegal.
"Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors," Bonta wrote.
Huang has agreed to testify before Congress after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.

item.title: Nvidia stock extends $2.7 trillion rout as SEC probe reportedly investigates its accounting
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Nvidia stock extends $2.7 trillion rout as SEC probe reportedly investigates its accounting
2026-11-21
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidia-stock-extends-25-trillion-rout-as-sec-probe-reportedly-investigates-its-accounting-194945274.html
Nvidia's worst week on record just got worse. Now the government is asking questions about its books.
Nvidia (NVDA) stock fell 14% Friday, its worst day since the DeepSeek rout in January 2025 and its seventh straight loss, before bouncing nearly 4% in after-hours trading. The drop came as Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission's probe of the chipmaker is examining potential accounting issues.
The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that the probe includes an examination of whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. Nvidia didn't respond to Bloomberg's request for comment on that report, and the SEC declined to comment.
The selling set records. Nvidia shed about $490 billion in market value Friday and nearly $900 billion this week, as its stock had its worst week since October 2008. That tops the $573 billion it lost last week, previously the biggest one-week drop for any company on record, according to Dow Jones Market Data.
Since its Oct. 6 record, Nvidia has lost about $2.7 trillion in market value, more than the $2.5 trillion that The Kobeissi Letter called the biggest 45-day loss for any stock in history. The world's most valuable company six weeks ago now ranks fourth in the US, behind Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOGL).
Nvidia's latest quarterly report raised a few questions. The company said its 10-Q, the detailed quarterly filing, would come "in the coming weeks" instead of the same evening as usual, and the release mentioned an ongoing investigation by an independent board committee.
Nvidia booked about $104 billion of revenue through its Singapore unit in 2025, roughly half its sales, the Financial Times reported. The Journal said the disclosure questions include Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer US officials suspect of rerouting its chips to China.
Nvidia's customers are also taking longer to pay, with bills outstanding at 64 days of sales, the most since 2022. It's not clear which of these, if any, the SEC is focused on.
Washington wants answers fast. "I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday, after Jensen Huang's exit as CEO. President Trump said Friday he "would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," while criticizing the chipmaker's new leadership.
California is digging in too. Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia Thursday, investigating whether its advanced chips reached China and whether the company misled investors. "Companies cannot mislead their investors," Bonta said.

item.title: 7 reasons why tech stocks are getting hammered again
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
7 reasons why tech stocks are getting hammered again
2026-11-21
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/7-reasons-why-tech-stocks-are-getting-hammered-again-183747857.html
So much for the much-hyped Anthropic (ANT) IPO on Thursday lifting the spirits of tech investors ahead of the holidays.
Lost in all the Anthropic IPO coverage yesterday was the fact that, while the stock finished up nicely on its debut day, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fell 2.2%.
The selling pressure in wider tech intensified on Friday, underpinned by several key reasons, pros say.
"This sell-off has been driven by a perfect storm," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives wrote.
He listed the catalysts for the latest tech rout: "1) The Blue Tidal Wave win and fears about an anti-AI/anti-datacenter DC, 2) losing the global leader of the AI Revolution Jensen in his black eye moment, 3) China driven regulatory concerns across the rest of semis/memory stocks (e.g. AMD short report yesterday), 4) multiple market clearing events which have just led to more selling, 5) Anthropic IPO being a massive success but marginally reducing liquidity from other tech names, 6) significant fund P&L pain diminishing buying power, and 7) sticky inflation and hawkish Fed speak with concerns around more hikes and constricting financial conditions."
Anthropic is getting roped into the sell-off in day two of public company life. Shares of the model builder dropped 12% in afternoon trading on Friday as investors booked profits after a frenetic first day of trading.
Follow live updates on the stock market sell-off
Anthropic made a monster debut on Wall Street Thursday, with shares opening at $111.50 a little before noon ET, a 34% premium to the $83 IPO price.
But the AI company's stock couldn't hold on to its early gains: The stock closed at $97.17, up 17% on the day.
That closing price gave Anthropic a market capitalization of about $1.28 trillion, or roughly $1.75 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
Wall Street is still out there defending tech stocks, especially at valuations not seen in years.
D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria said a "clean" earnings report from Nvidia (NVDA) this week and a successful Anthropic IPO "clear the way for AI-driven stocks to start coming back."
Ives added, "We continue to believe a diversified AI approach to the market is the way to own the winners and derivatives of the AI Revolution into 2027: This is a painful tech sell-off that is heavily discounting this 4th Industrial Revolution thesis will take place over the next few years … and that is the wrong move in our view."

Ives added, "We continue to believe a diversified AI approach to the market is the way to own the winners and derivatives of the AI Revolution into 2027: This is a painful tech sell-off that is heavily discounting this 4th Industrial Revolution thesis will take place over the next few years … and that is the wrong move in our view."

item.title: Anthropic engineer's warning about Claude Code explains why tech outages could get much worse
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Anthropic engineer's warning about Claude Code explains why tech outages could get much worse
2026-11-21
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/anthropic-engineers-warning-about-claude-code-explains-why-tech-outages-could-get-much-worse-110000573.html
There have been so many prominent tech services experiencing outages lately that the problems have gone mainstream in a new way we haven't seen before.
As we wrote recently, the problems are far more than just cybersecurity, though AI means hackers can discover and exploit bugs like never before. Infrastructure is decrepit. Maintenance is deferred. Exhausted, too-small teams of IT workers aren't up to this level of chaos.
But there's another explanation that's perhaps underappreciated: one big downside of Claude Code, the marquee product that has given Anthropic (ANT) its trillion-dollar valuation.
The problem is best explained by someone who would know best: a prominent Anthropic engineer (and former Google engineer) who works on Claude Code as a member of the technical staff, Addy Osmani, whose treatise on "comprehension debt" bounced around the software engineering community in March — and is even more relevant today.
What Osmani highlights isn't really a weakness in Claude Code, but in how companies and engineering teams use it. The gist: AI can write code faster than we can review it. The speed is a great benefit, but it's also a curse, as myriad companies pivot from writing code to overseeing teams of AI agents that complain less and write more.
As Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said this week, the company's engineers "build a software factory that builds the product. They don't build the product."
Traditionally, the laborious process of checking other people's code is how software engineers internalize why systems are designed the way they are, and why decisions from earlier in a project might be meaningful today.
But reviewing the entirety of AI code isn't feasible given how fast we can produce it now. It's too unwieldy, and this represents a massive bottleneck for progress. Tests, AI review, and spending less time reviewing can be effective. But they've removed layers of verification, and ultimately comprehension, which is disappearing, Osmani explains.
All this means that with code piling up faster than humans can review it, companies can lose control of their systems in a way far more prosaic and banal than some sort of sentient AI or Skynet doomsday scenario.

item.title: Treasuries Eye Longest Rally in Five Months on Haven Demand
item.author: Matthew Burgess; David Finnerty
item.description:
Treasuries Eye Longest Rally in Five Months on Haven Demand
2026-11-21
Por Matthew Burgess; David Finnerty
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/treasuries-eye-longest-rally-five-043323098.html
(Bloomberg) -- Treasuries are headed for their longest rally in almost five months, as mounting doubts over the artificial intelligence trade deepen a global stock selloff and drive investors toward haven assets.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Yields fell between two and three basis points across the curve in Asia on Friday, putting a gauge of Treasury returns on track for a fifth day of gains, matching the longest rally since June 29. A Bloomberg gauge of the dollar is set for its fourth straight weekly gain.
The risk-off turn is adding momentum to the Treasury rally as investors reassess lofty AI valuations and the vast spending underpinning the boom. Global stocks are poised for their longest losing streak in more than three years. With doubts over the trade spilling into broader markets, haven demand could keep yields under pressure.
"Steady falls in yields today, alongside weakness in the key Asian equity indices and US futures do point to a continuation of the risk-off moves that started overnight," said Kenneth Crompton, head of rates strategy at National Australia Bank.
Yields remain elevated despite the latest moves, with the 10-year rate nearing its longest stretch above 5% in almost two decades, reflecting concerns about sticky inflation and expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes through next year.
While investors are wanting to cut some risk, "we don't see the AI trade as being entirely derailed," said Crompton. "The fundamental case for 10-year US Treasuries to rally well through 5% is weak."
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.
